additions.text: Reports mild tingling in fingers, possibly due to swelling; sensation in fingers intact.
additions.why: Neurovascular symptoms after a distal radius fracture are safety relevant and need a documented baseline.

additions.text: Vitals: BP 140/70, HR 80, T 97.2, RR 20; BP elevation likely pain related.
additions.why: Vital signs and the mildly elevated blood pressure are relevant before surgery.

additions.text: Pain with radial/ulnar deviation; unable to make a tight fist.

additions.why: Pain characteristics help rule out associated injuries and guide comfort measures.

it's just really really bad when i move it all

follow_up_questions.question: Is the tingling getting worse, and have your fingers looked pale or blue, felt cold, or become harder to move?
follow_up_questions.why: Progressive neurovascular symptoms can signal median nerve compression or compartment syndrome needing urgent care.

follow_up_questions.question: Do you have any medication allergies, and what other medicines do you take, such as antidepressants or blood thinners?
follow_up_questions.why: Allergies and interactions matter before starting tramadol and before surgery.

follow_up_questions.question: Did you hit your head or hurt anywhere else when you fell on the stairs?
follow_up_questions.why: A fall on stairs can cause other injuries that were not assessed.

follow_up_questions.question: Have you had any problems with anesthesia before, or any conditions like osteoporosis or bleeding problems?
follow_up_questions.why: Surgical risk and bone health affect operative planning.
